claims.text: Combining PGM catalysts with cobalt-rich spinel oxide supports can enhance methane oxidation activity relative to conventional formulations.
The cobalt-rich spinel intervention will improve catalyst durability.
The cobalt-rich spinel intervention will permit a reduction in PGM loading without loss of performance.
PGM and spinel oxides can be combined in a layered catalyst architecture.
NiCo2O4 is a suitable example of the proposed cobalt-rich spinel support.
The proposed catalyst is applicable to methane oxidation under stoichiometric natural-gas-engine exhaust conditions.
The benefit should hold specifically in a sub-500 °C operating window.
Atmospheres that periodically regenerate oxygen vacancies are required for the proposed benefit.
Bulk oxygen-vacancy formation energy is a useful descriptor of the direct and indirect roles of reducible spinel oxides in PGM methane-oxidation catalysts.
Favorable oxygen-vacancy formation energy correlates with dynamic oxygen-storage capacity.
The spinel support forms a robust interface with PGM nanoparticles.
The reducible spinel contributes directly to oxidation through oxygen-vacancy-related or lattice-oxygen chemistry.
The spinel indirectly promotes more efficient methane activation at PGM sites.
PGM/spinel layered architectures lower methane light-off temperature T50.
The modified catalyst will sustain catalytic performance over extended operation better than a PGM-on-inert-oxide baseline.
Enhanced oxygen mobility will allow lower PGM consumption while maintaining or increasing activity and durability.
Computational screening identifies NiCo2O4 as having optimally tuned oxygen-vacancy formation energy for this application.
The benefit may fail when temperature or exhaust composition deviates substantially from the tested regime.
